documents.note: Six of the eight clause types, two at the highest band, in ordinary contract prose. The .txt, .pdf and .docx entries carry the same prose in three files; each is counted once below.
Multi-column, hyphenated at line ends, ligature-heavy, running header and footer, and one sentence split across a page boundary.
The same six sentences as Word paragraphs. No pages and no line breaks, so it isolates the character rule from the layout repair.
Superscript footnote markers inside body lines, footnote blocks under a rule at the foot of each page, and one labelled clause that lives in a footnote rather than in the body.
A three-column fee table with gutters wide enough to read as columns, one whole sentence inside a cell, and prose above and below it.

Carries the two clause types no other document in the corpus does: non-compete and non-solicit, and termination and notice. Two separate non-compete clauses, so one clause type has to produce two flags.
A guarantee with a consent to judgment, two separate uncapped indemnities, a one-way cap that strips remedies, and no way out before the end of a sixty-month term.
Handles all eight topics fairly rather than omitting them, which makes it a harder all-clear than a document that says nothing about them.
A second all-clear document, shorter and in a different trade, so an all-clear is not measured against a single piece of prose.

Out of scope for analysis (ADR 0002). The harness extracts it and reports it as not analysed: what Redline returns for an adhesion contract is ticket 07's to decide, and one of the five questions PRD.md section 8 leaves open.
